title: Making HTTP Requests with cURL
learning_outcomes: Explain what making http requests with curl contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: curl initialization.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: API integrations cross a network boundary where responses can be slow, malformed, unauthorized, duplicated, or unavailable. Check status and content, set timeouts, and make retries and webhook processing safe to repeat. In this lesson, focus on curl initialization; then compare it with request methods. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use making http requests with curl when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
